newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures gyrate to lower close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures gyrate to lower close.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures spent the afternoon gyrating at mostly lower levels and ended moderately active trading lower.

Floor brokers said a fund bought some 400 March Standard & Poor's 500 futures near the 764.00 level during the final minutes, helping the contract cut losses and persuading locals who were short to capitulate as well.

Some brokers called the day's trade largely technical in nature, with nearby S&Ps swinging near a support point at the 761.60 area after proving unable to catch a bid from a final uptick in U.S. Treasury bond futures near their close.

"It was mostly technical," a floor broker said of the afternoon's trade. "I think locals were looking to press that area (761.60)...because we didn't get the reaction we wanted" when T-bonds firmed late.
But the late push lower, like most of the day's swings, lacked solid followthrough as traders remained noncommittal ahead of a spate of U.S. economic data this week.

December U.S. consumer prices Tuesday are expected to rise 0.3 percent overall and gain 0.2 percent in the core rate. Retail sales are seen gaining 0.5 percent and increasing 0.4 percent excluding autos.
Traders also noted some signs of small, periodic arbitrage sell programs during the market's downward swings, when the premium shrank to 4.10 points or less.

Early Monday, March S&P 500s advanced on the coattails of Friday's upside reversal and drew small arbitrage buy programs, which needed about 5.90 points over cash, when the premium had yawned to more than 9.00 points.

Traders said they saw no reaction to morning news that Fidelity Investments said its Magellan fund cut its holdings in equities to 88.5 percent of total assets at the end of November from 89.8 percent a month earlier.

The March Nikkei index futures rallied, with most volume concentrated during the first minutes of trade, floor brokers said. The contract shaved its biggest gains, however, after it failed to muster enough strength to sustain a rise above resistance at the 18,000 level.

March S&Ps settled down 2.30 points at 764.30, Value Lines lost 2.05 points to 697.15, Nikkei 225 jumped 635.0 to 17,900.0, Midcap 400 lost 1.85 to 262.15, NYSE Composite fell 1.50 to 403.20, Russell 2000 lost 1.25 to 368.25, and NASDAQ 100 futures slumped 3.75 points to 872.25.
